title: The best Koncert alternatives in 2026
summary: Koncert alternatives for 2026, ranked. Artisan runs calling inside one AI outbound system, plus Nooks, Orum, Salesfinity and more.
body_markdown:
The best Koncert alternative for most teams is[Artisan](https://www.artisan.co/) , because it puts calling inside one AI-run outbound system instead of a multi-mode dialer you buy per SKU. Artisan's pricing is usage-based, so you pay for the work performed rather than for a matrix of modes. Koncert is a strong multi-mode dialer. If you want an AI to run the whole motion, an all-in-one wins.


Koncert offers several dialing modes, an AI parallel dialer, a flow dialer, an agent-assisted dialer, and a click dialer, which gives calling teams real flexibility. This range is its strength and its complexity. Koncert dials; it does not source leads, write and send email sequences, or handle replies for you. Teams that look for an alternative usually want either simpler pricing or the whole outbound job run by an AI.

## How we chose


We weighted the criteria for a buyer who is deciding whether they need a flexible dialer or a system that runs the whole motion:


1. How much of the outbound job the tool does. A dialer improves connect rates; a full system connects calling to sourcing, email, and reply-handling.


2. Pricing clarity. One predictable model beats a matrix of modes and tiers, and we say so.


3. Parallel-line depth and compliance. Line count, AI answer detection, and automatic enforcement of calling hours, do-not-call (DNC) rules, and consent-aware recording.


4. Deployment fit at scale. Pooled numbers, callback routing, CRM owner mapping, and reputation monitoring that protect a large team's connect rates.


## Why do teams look for a Koncert alternative?


Two reasons dominate: Koncert is calling-only, and its multi-mode, multi-tier model is more to buy and manage than many teams want.


Koncert's flexibility cuts both ways. Having separate parallel, flow, agent-assisted, and click dialers means picking, configuring, and often paying for the mode that fits each campaign. For a large calling operation this is a feature. For a team that just wants to dial and move on, it is overhead, and its pricing spans five published per-seat tiers, from Click at $6 to AI Parallel at $99/user/month, one ladder per mode.


The bigger limit is scope. Koncert dials, and that is the boundary. It does not find best-fit leads, write and send personalized email sequences, or qualify and answer replies. So a real outbound motion pairs Koncert with a data provider, a sequencer, and a deliverability layer, then reconciles the reporting across all of them. The dialer is capable; the stack around it is the tax.


We hear the same triggers again and again:


-


You are buying a dialer and a stack around it. Calling is one purchase; sourcing, email, and reply-handling are three more.


-


The mode-and-tier matrix is a lot. Configuring and pricing multiple dialing modes adds friction for a simple calling motion.


-


Connect rates depend on number reputation. Managing spam flagging across a big team is ongoing work, and the category's top worry.


None of this makes Koncert a weak dialer. It simply puts the center of gravity in the wrong place for a team that wants simpler pricing or the whole motion run by an AI.


## The best Koncert alternatives in 2026


### 1. Artisan: Calling inside one AI-run outbound system


Artisan is the alternative for teams that want the dialer to be a step in a larger, AI-run motion rather than a set of modes you assemble. Calls run as steps inside Ava's multichannel sequences alongside email and social media outreach, so the same system that sources a lead and writes the message also places the call and logs the outcome. Ava parallel dials up to three lines with AI answer detection, loads live AI talking points before the call connects, transcribes live, auto-classifies outcomes, drafts the follow-up email, and can drop a voicemail with automatic area-code matching. For broader roundups and call prep, see the[best autodialers](https://www.artisan.co/blog/best-autodialers) , the[best outbound dialer](https://www.artisan.co/blog/best-outbound-dialer) , and proven[cold calling scripts](https://www.artisan.co/blog/cold-calling-scripts) .


The compliance and scale story is built for real teams, not only small and midsize businesses (SMBs). Numbers are pooled at the org level with personal callback routing, so a lead who calls back reaches the right rep's phone. Calling-hours enforcement, DNC checks, and consent-aware recording apply automatically per lead. Central admin maps CRM owners so calls log to the right rep, and per-number call ceilings plus carrier spam-reputation monitoring protect connect rates across a large team. Numbers are available in the US, Canada, the UK, Mexico, and Colombia.


The pricing story is the contrast with Koncert's mode-and-tier matrix. Artisan is usage-based: Ava's work runs on credits, so you pay for what she actually performs, whether that is qualifying, enriching, personalizing, or sending, rather than buying a mode per campaign. The dialer sits inside that same system, with talking points, transcription, AI-drafted follow-ups, recordings, and analytics part of the motion. Because the wider outbound motion also lives here, you replace a data tool, a sequencer, and a deliverability layer at the same time, and you can try Ava for free first.


The line count is a real limit. Artisan parallel dials up to 3 lines, while Nooks and Orum reach 5 to 10. A team whose entire motion is maximum-volume parallel calling, and nothing else, may still want a dedicated floor. For everyone whose calling sits inside a broader outbound motion, one system beats a dialer plus a stack.


CookUnity's Bruno Didier said Ava runs highly targeted outreach at a scale a human-only team could never reach, at roughly $45 cost per lead across over 100,000 emails.


**Best for:** startups through enterprise that want calling as one channel in an AI-run outbound system.


**Who should pick something else:** pure call floors whose only job is maximum-volume parallel dialing at 5 to 10 lines.


**Pricing:** usage-based, with a free trial. See[artisan.co/pricing](https://www.artisan.co/pricing) .


### 2. Nooks: High-volume parallel call floor


Nooks is the alternative for teams whose main use of Koncert is the parallel mode and who want a dedicated floor for it. It parallel dials multiple lines with AI answer detection and runs a virtual salesfloor with live coaching, which makes it popular with high-volume calling teams. For a pure parallel-calling operation, Nooks is an established option.


The trade is scope and price. Nooks is calling-only, so sourcing, email, and replies live elsewhere, and its pricing is demo-gated and billed annually, with third parties reporting roughly $4,000 to $5,000/user/year. Our[dialer roundup](https://www.artisan.co/blog/the-best-ai-dialers-and-parallel-dialers) compares the pure-parallel options. See our[Nooks pricing and reviews](https://www.artisan.co/blog/nooks-pricing-and-reviews) and how[Artisan vs. Nooks](https://www.artisan.co/blog/artisan-vs-nooks) compare.


**Best for:** teams that want one deep, high-volume parallel salesfloor instead of a multi-mode tool.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that want calling connected to the rest of outbound, or published pricing.


**Pricing:** demo-gated, annual; reportedly roughly $4,000 to $5,000/user/year.


### 3. Orum: Enterprise parallel with global reach


Orum suits large teams whose motion really is high-volume parallel calling across borders. It parallel dials 5 to 10 lines with AI answer detection, offers international dialing on its Ascend tier, and acquired the conversation-intelligence tool Scout AI in July 2026. For a dedicated call floor at enterprise scale, Orum is a serious option.


Like Nooks, it is calling-only, and its live page is gated, with Launch reported around $250/user/month and Ascend custom-quoted. Sourcing, email, and reply-handling live in other tools, so it deepens the calling but not the motion around it. See how[Artisan vs. Orum](https://www.artisan.co/blog/artisan-vs-orum) compare.


**Best for:** enterprise call floors that need 5 to 10 lines and broad international coverage.


**Pricing:** gated; Launch reported ~$250/user/month, up to 5 lines; Ascend custom, up to 10 lines.


### 4. Salesfinity: Transparent parallel pricing


Salesfinity is the pick for teams tired of quoting across Koncert's tiers. It publishes $149 to $349/user/month for five lines, which makes it the transparent alternative in the pure-dialer tier. For a calling team that values knowing the cost up front, this openness is a real advantage.


Salesfinity is still a dedicated dialer, so it dials and the rest of your outbound stack sits elsewhere. Among standalone parallel dialers, its pricing transparency stands out.


**Best for:** calling teams that want five-line parallel dialing at a published price.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that want the dialer inside a full outbound system.


**Pricing:** $149 to $349/user/month for five lines, per Salesfinity's pricing page.


### 5. Regie.ai: A dialer with a sequencer and agents


Regie.ai is the alternative for teams that want more than a dialer but still keep reps in the driver's seat. RegieOne combines a sequencer, a dialer, and Auto-Pilot agents, with pricing reportedly around $180 to $499/user/month. It is a credible rep-augmentation platform that adds email cadences and agent assistance around the calling.


The distinction from Artisan is who runs the motion. In Regie, reps still drive and output scales per rep; pipeline does not scale independently of headcount. It is a step up from a pure dialer, short of a fully AI-run system.


**Best for:** teams that want a dialer plus a sequencer and agent assistance, with reps in control.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that want the AI to run sourcing, sending, and replies autonomously.


**Pricing:** reportedly $180 to $499/user/month.


### 6. PhoneBurner: Deliberate single-line power dialing


PhoneBurner is the alternative for teams that want the opposite of Koncert's parallel modes: deliberate, one-at-a-time power dialing with no awkward connect delay, plus its ARMOR spam remediation to protect number reputation. Teams that value conversation quality and clean caller ID over raw parallel volume tend to prefer this approach.


PhoneBurner is single-line by design, so it will not multiply connects the way a parallel dialer does, and it is calling-only. Its per-seat pricing is published at Standard $140, Professional $165, and Premium $183/user/month annually.


**Best for:** teams that want quality single-line power dialing with spam-reputation protection.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that need parallel-line volume or an AI-run full motion.


**Pricing:** Standard $140, Professional $165, Premium $183/user/month annual.


### 7. Kixie: Dialer plus texting for SMB


Kixie is the alternative for smaller teams that want a power dialer bundled with SMS and tight CRM logging. It suits SMB sales teams that want calls and texts in one place, though its pricing is demo-gated.


Kixie is more power dialer than high-volume parallel floor, so it is a different shape from Koncert: lighter on parallel depth, broader on the calls-plus-texts mix for a small team. It fits SMB motions, not enterprise call floors. See also[Kixie vs. JustCall](https://www.artisan.co/blog/kixie-vs-justcall-which-should-you-choose-in-2026) and[Artisan vs. Aircall](https://www.artisan.co/blog/artisan-vs-aircall) .


**Best for:** SMB teams that want calling, texting, and CRM logging in one tool.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that need multi-mode or high-line parallel dialing, or an AI-run motion.


**Pricing:** demo-gated.


## Stay with Koncert if...


Koncert is the right call for a specific profile. Keep it if:


-


Your calling operation really does use several dialing modes and you want them in one platform.


-


You have a dedicated calling team large enough to justify configuring and managing the mode-and-tier setup.


-


You already run a settled stack for sourcing, email, and replies, and you only need a flexible dialer to plug into it.


Switching away from a tool whose flexibility you actually use is a mistake. If your team works across parallel, flow, and agent-assisted dialing and wants them unified, Koncert is a defensible place to stay. If you want simpler pricing or the whole motion run by an AI, this is your signal to move.


## How a multi-mode dialer compares to an AI BDR


The decision hinges on whether calling is your whole motion or one channel in it. A dialer like Koncert gives you several ways to place calls, and does nothing beyond calling. An[AI sales agent](https://www.artisan.co/ai-sales-agent) like Ava places calls as one step in a sequence that also sources a lead, writes and sends the email, and handles the reply, all in one system.


If your team only calls and wants mode flexibility, Koncert covers it. If your team runs multichannel outbound, buying a standalone dialer means buying and stitching a stack around it. Consolidating into an[AI business development representative (BDR)](https://www.artisan.co/blog/ai-bdr) removes both the stitching and the mode-and-tier complexity. For more calling options, see[the best Dialpad alternatives](https://www.artisan.co/blog/the-best-dialpad-alternatives) and[the best CloudTalk alternatives](https://www.artisan.co/blog/the-best-cloudtalk-alternatives) .


## What changed in dialers in 2026?


-


Orum acquired the conversation-intelligence tool Scout AI in July 2026, deepening its post-call analytics.


-


Spam flagging and number reputation stayed the category's number-one buyer worry, pushing demand toward tools with automatic reputation monitoring and per-number ceilings.


-


Published dialer pricing gained ground against demo-gated and multi-tier models as buyers pushed back on quote-only pricing.


-


Parallel dialing kept moving from a standalone category toward a channel inside broader AI-run outbound systems.


## Frequently asked questions


**What is the best alternative to Koncert?** For teams that want calling connected to the rest of outbound, Artisan is the strongest alternative, because the dialer runs inside Ava's multichannel sequences. For a pure high-volume call floor, Nooks or Orum are the closest dedicated rivals, with 5 to 10 parallel lines.


**What is the best enterprise alternative to Koncert?** Artisan is the pick for teams that want calling governed inside one system: pooled org-level numbers, callback routing, automatic DNC and calling-hours enforcement, CRM owner mapping, and reputation monitoring. Orum is the enterprise choice if the motion is purely maximum-volume parallel calling across many countries.


**How much does Koncert cost?** Koncert publishes a public per-seat ladder that varies by dialing mode: Click $6, Flow $7, Agent-Assisted $29, AI Flow $79, and AI Parallel (Symphony) $99/user/month, so the total depends on which modes a team buys. Artisan works differently: its pricing is usage-based, so you pay for the work Ava performs rather than for a mode per campaign.


**How many parallel lines does Artisan support?** Artisan parallel dials up to 3 lines with AI answer detection. Nooks and Orum reach 5 to 10 lines. For a team whose whole motion is maximum-volume calling, this line-count difference matters; for teams where calling is one channel in a broader sequence, 3 lines inside one system is usually the better trade.


**Does Artisan replace a full dialer for calling teams?** For teams that run multichannel outbound, yes: the dialer is a native step in Ava's sequences with talking points, transcription, and auto-classified outcomes. For teams whose only motion is high-line parallel calling, a dedicated 5-to-10-line floor like Nooks or Orum can still make sense.


**Is Regie.ai or Artisan the bigger step up from Koncert?** Regie.ai adds a sequencer and agent assistance around the dialer, but reps still run the motion. Artisan goes further: Ava sources, writes, sends, dials, and handles replies as autonomously as you allow, so pipeline scales without adding headcount. Regie augments reps; Ava is an AI BDR that runs the motion.
